name: KMS key-policy account-root delegation ('Enable IAM User Permissions', suite-2 test 51)
note: IAM-1205 / acceptance-suite-2 test 51. The standard KMS key-policy statement grants Principal {AWS: arn:aws:iam::111122223333:root} kms:* on Resource:* for a key OWNED by account 111122223333. This must be read as an ACCOUNT DELEGATION to the owning account (the account and its IAM-empowered administrators), NOT public access (the principal is one account, not '*') and NOT root-user-only (the ':root' account principal represents the account and its admins). Per KMS semantics the account-principal statement does not itself grant any individual IAM principal use of the key; it ALLOWS the account to delegate access via IAM identity policies, so which principals are actually reachable is UNKNOWN without those policies. Resource:'*' in a key policy means THIS attached key only, never every KMS key in the account - and the analyzer builds NO graph node per key (graphEdgeTypes is empty). The finding must be RESOURCE-KMS-ACCOUNT-DELEGATION, never PUBLIC-ACCESS, RESOURCE-CROSS-ACCOUNT, RESOURCE-SAME-ACCOUNT-GRANT, or any identity-style broad-resource / kms:* finding.

RESOURCE-KMS-ACCOUNT-DELEGATION: every KMS key in the account
